s: Inspects HTTP traffic against attack signatures (SQLi, XSS, bots) before requests touch your services.
w: Operating inline or as a mirror, it matches requests against managed rule sets (OWASP Top 10, bot lists, reputation feeds), geoblocks, and rate heuristics. Matches trigger allow/count/block actions. Tuning is continuous: false positives break real users, false negatives let attacks through.
use: Public-facing apps needing baseline OWASP protection at the edge
Compliance mandates (PCI-DSS requires WAF for card-handling surfaces)
Blocking credential-stuffing and scraping bot waves
Emergency virtual patching while a framework CVE fix rolls out
avoid: Business-logic abuse (e.g., 'user A transferring to themselves twice') - needs app-level rules
Replacing authN/authZ - WAF sees patterns, not identity semantics
Highly custom APIs where generic signatures mostly generate noise

pat.d: WAF at edge + input validation in services + least-privilege DB accounts - no single wall trusts itself.

pits: False positives blocking legit traffic - start in count mode, tune, then enforce
Regex catastrophic backtracking under crafted payloads - prefer managed rules with safe engines
tips: Frame as buy-down of known vulnerability classes; emphasize monitoring mode rollout discipline
